chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Treat your sick ones with charity, repel afflictions with supplication, and draw down sustenance with charity. For indeed it passes through the jaws of seven hundred devils, and there is nothing heavier upon Satan than charity given to a believer, and it falls into the Hand of the Lord, Blessed and Exalted, before it falls into the hand of the servant.'

key_terms.البلاء: Bala' — affliction, tribulation, or divine trial sent upon a person
key_terms.الرب: Al-Rabb — the Lord, God as Sustainer and Master
key_terms.الرزق: Rizq — sustenance, livelihood, provision from God
key_terms.الصدقة: Sadaqa — voluntary charity given for God's sake, distinct from obligatory zakat
key_terms.لحيّ: Luhiyy — jaws/beards of the devils, indicating forceful passage through demonic obstruction

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the spiritual benefits of sadaqa (charity)?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) teaches three spiritual remedies: using charity to heal the sick, using supplication to ward off tribulations, and using charity to attract provision. He emphasizes charity's spiritual potency by describing how it forces its way through seven hundred devils — indicating the immense opposition satanic forces mount against acts of generosity — and how charity is received by God Himself before it reaches the human recipient, signifying divine acceptance and reward.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Abdullah Bin Al Qasim, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Treat your sick ones with the charity and repel the afflictions with the supplication, and cause the sustenance to descend with the charity.  Charity finds its way through the beards of seven hundred devils, and there is nothing heavier upon the Satan<sup>la</sup> than the charity upon the Believer, and it falls into the Hand of the Lord<sup>azwj</sup> Blessed and High before it falls into the hand of the servant’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Qasim, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘Cure your illnesses by giving charity, repel misfortunes with prayer, and allow means of sustenance to descend upon you by giving charity. Charity finds its way through the beards of seven hundred Satans. No other thing is heavier upon Satan than when you give charity to a believing person. It finds its place in the hand of the Lord, the Most Blessed, the Most High, before finding its place in the hand of a servant (of Allah).”’
